questionText: Which of the following is a political consequence of globalization?

options.text:
Globalisation has encouraged the interaction between different cultures
leading to cultural heterogenisation.
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text:
Globalisation results in reduction of state capacity to take decisions on its
own.
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies the chronological/logical progression.

options.text: Globalisation generates cultural homogenisation across the globe.
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text:
Globalisation has produced unequal development across countries and
regions of the world.
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
NCERT Class 12 Contemporary World Politics (Chapter 9: Globalisation, 'Political Consequences'): 'Globalisation results in an erosion of state capacity, that is, the ability of government to do what they do. All over the world, the old 'welfare state' is now giving way to a more minimalist state that performs certain core functions such as the maintenance of law and order and the security of its citizens. In place of the state, the market becomes the prime determinant of economic and social priorities.'
Hence, option (B) is correct.
